<thought>Using the molecular formula C14H11O6, the double bond equivalents (DBE) are calculated by the standard formula DBE = (2C + 2 - H)/2, ignoring O. Substituting the values gives DBE = (2*14 + 2 - 11)/2 = (28 + 2 - 11)/2 = 19/2 = 9.5. Since DBE must be an integer, the compound likely has a radical or charge, but the integer part is 9.</thought>
<final_answer>9</final_answer>
